title: Northwind Analytics - POC check-in (performance + stability)
summary: Northwind shared results from the last 7 days of their POC load test. Median and p95 latencies improved vs their baseline, but they still see intermittent p99 spikes during bursty traffic and mixed prompt length distributions. Redwood linked the spikes to KV cache fragmentation behavior observed in canary and explained the upcoming KV compaction + tier-aware eviction rollout plan and guardrails (budgets, metrics, kill-switch). Northwind confirmed remaining blockers are stability under bursts, clear rollback triggers, and a retest window once the canary is expanded. Agreed to rerun the benchmark after compaction canary reaches their hosted cohort and to align on success criteria for moving to Dedicated/VPC next.
topics: POC status and success criteria (p95/p99, error rate, throughput)
Observed tail-latency spikes during burst + mixed sequence lengths
KV cache fragmentation signals and new metrics dashboard requirements
Compaction canary expansion timeline and rollback guardrails
Next retest plan and decision checkpoint for Dedicated capacity
next_steps: Redwood (Paula) to share the updated compaction canary schedule and confirm when Northwind’s org is in cohort.
Redwood (Allison) to send metric name/definitions for fragmentation ratio, bytes moved, compaction time, and eviction counters; include dashboard panel screenshots.
Redwood (Sean) to send proposed automated rollback triggers (p99 delta, error rate, compaction budget saturation) and who flips the kill-switch.
Northwind (Priya/Jordan) to rerun the burst + mixed-length benchmark within 48 hours of cohort enablement and share raw trace IDs + workload parameters.
Follow-up call to review retest results and decide if POC advances to Dedicated/VPC scope.
action_items: Paula Mendes: Email canary cohort timing + retest window options to Northwind (by 2026-02-06).
Allison Grant: Send metrics standard + dashboard panel list and links (by 2026-02-06).
Sean Gallagher: Send guardrails/rollback criteria + escalation path for kill-switch (by 2026-02-07).
Priya Desai: Run updated load test after compaction enablement and share results + trace exemplars (target 2026-02-10).
transcript:
Northwind Analytics - POC check-in (performance + stability)
Recorded: 2026-02-05 10:07 AM PT
Duration: 42 minutes

Attendees
- Paula Mendes (Redwood Inference)
- Sean Gallagher (Redwood Inference)
- Omar El-Sayed (Redwood Inference)
- Allison Grant (Redwood Inference)
- Priya Desai (Northwind Analytics)
- Jordan Lee (Northwind Analytics)
- Megan Chen (Northwind Analytics)


[00:00] Paula Mendes: Alright, I think we’re recording. Hi everyone. Thanks for making the time. This is our weekly POC check-in, focus today on performance stability and where we are on the tail latency spikes. Priya, Jordan, Megan — anything you want to add to the agenda?

[00:16] Priya Desai: That’s it. We have numbers from the last week, and I want to make sure we’re aligned on what “good” looks like for the next retest.

[00:24] Jordan Lee: Yeah and specifically, like, what the rollback triggers are when you guys flip the canary wider. We had one pretty gnarly p99 event Tuesday night.

[00:33] Paula Mendes: Yep, we’ll get into that. Sean and Omar are on, and Allison for metrics. Megan, anything?

[00:40] Megan Chen: Mostly I want to understand if this is a known issue with the runtime or if it’s something in our harness. We need to give our leadership a date for when we can make a call.

[00:51] Paula Mendes: Totally. So maybe start with your readout. Priya, do you want to walk through the results?

[01:00] Priya Desai: Sure. So we ran the same workload profile as last week. It’s like 70% chat, 20% summarization, 10% “tool” style responses. Mixed prompt length — we have a long tail. We also injected bursts, like traffic ramps 4x for two minutes, then back down.

[01:18] Priya Desai: Improvements: median is down, and p95 is down. I don’t have the exact medians in my head, but it’s like, we’re consistently under our p95 target during steady state.

[01:28] Priya Desai: The issue is p99. We still see occasional spikes. Not constant, but when it happens it’s, you know, it blows our SLO. And we also saw one run where we started getting “over capacity” type errors — not a ton, but enough to notice.

[01:45] Paula Mendes: Got it. When you say “blows SLO,” what number are you using for p99?

[01:49] Priya Desai: For this POC, we’re trying to keep p99 under 1.2 seconds for 256-ish output tokens. The spikes hit 2.5 to 3 seconds, like brief.

[02:02] Jordan Lee: And to be clear, that’s not our whole product SLO, that’s the one we’re evaluating for your endpoint.

[02:07] Sean Gallagher: That’s helpful. Do you see it correlated with the burst windows or random?

[02:12] Priya Desai: Mostly burst windows. Also when we have more long prompts in the mix. Like we did one run with a heavier long-context distribution and it got worse.

[02:23] Omar El-Sayed: Okay, that matches what we’ve been seeing internally. Sorry, quick question — are you pinning to a single model version right now?

[02:30] Priya Desai: Yes. We pinned to the one you recommended, the “-instruct” variant. Same as last week.

[02:35] Omar El-Sayed: Great.

[02:36] Paula Mendes: Jordan, you mentioned Tuesday night. Was that in your load harness or actual app traffic?

[02:42] Jordan Lee: Harness. We ran it in staging, but it’s intended to mirror production. Tuesday we got this cluster of p99 events over like 15 minutes. It looked like a sawtooth — we’d be fine, then bam, then fine. We grabbed trace IDs and some logs.

[02:56] Paula Mendes: Perfect, we’ll want those trace IDs.

[02:58] Allison Grant: And the timeframe, because we can line it up with compaction metrics on our side, even if you don’t have them yet.

[03:04] Priya Desai: Yeah. I can paste it after the call.

[03:07] Paula Mendes: Cool. So, Omar, maybe you give the “what we think is happening” summary, and then Sean on guardrails.

[03:15] Omar El-Sayed: Yep. So — and I’ll keep it short — the likely culprit is KV cache fragmentation under mixed sequence lengths and churn. When you have long-lived allocations mixed with many short ones, the allocator ends up with free space that’s not contiguous enough for the next request’s KV pages, and we pay overhead either trying to find pages or we do opportunistic evictions at a bad time.

[03:38] Omar El-Sayed: That can show up as tail latency spikes during decode, especially when the scheduler is already under pressure from bursts.

[03:46] Jordan Lee: Sorry, when you say “KV,” you mean like key/value attention cache, right?

[03:49] Omar El-Sayed: Exactly. The attention KV cache.

[03:52] Priya Desai: And your plan is the compaction thing?

[03:55] Omar El-Sayed: Right. We’ve built a compaction mechanism that relocates KV blocks incrementally, budgeted, so it doesn’t stall decode. And there’s a tier-aware eviction policy when we genuinely need to reclaim space.

[04:10] Omar El-Sayed: The important part: it’s behind a feature flag and we’re rolling it out in canary cohorts. Your org is not yet in the cohort — that’s why you’re still seeing the old behavior.

[04:20] Megan Chen: So we basically need to wait for the canary expansion to see if it fixes our main blocker.

[04:26] Paula Mendes: That’s the current plan, yes.

[04:28] Sean Gallagher: And we’re doing it with pretty strict guardrails. We’re not going to just flip it on and hope.

[04:33] Priya Desai: What’s the timeline for when we’d be included?

[04:36] Paula Mendes: We’re aiming for early next week for the next expansion step. I don’t want to promise a day on this call without checking the release train and SRE approvals. But it’s “days,” not “weeks.”

[04:48] Jordan Lee: Is it in prod at all?

[04:50] Sean Gallagher: It’s in internal canary and a small hosted subset. Not broadly across all hosted traffic. We had one canary incident — short-lived — and we tightened rollback conditions and budgets.

[05:03] Megan Chen: That’s the incident we saw referenced in the email chain?

[05:06] Paula Mendes: Yeah, exactly. It was a latency spike; we rolled back that cohort, fixed an edge case, and resumed. That’s why we’re being conservative.

[05:16] Priya Desai: Okay. So in the meantime, are there knobs we can tweak to reduce the p99 spikes? Like lower concurrency, or…?

[05:24] Omar El-Sayed: You can reduce burst concurrency, which reduces scheduler pressure, but it’s not really a fix. Another mitigation is to avoid mixing extremely long prompts with the burst windows, but I know that’s not realistic.

[05:38] Jordan Lee: Yeah we can’t. That’s basically our users.

[05:41] Allison Grant: What we can do now is make sure we’re measuring the right signals so when compaction is enabled we can be confident it’s not introducing new issues.

[05:50] Paula Mendes: Allison, can you outline what you’ll send?

[05:53] Allison Grant: Sure. We have standardized metric names for: fragmentation ratio (allocator health), bytes moved by compaction, compaction time, eviction counters (by reason), and also correlation panels against p95/p99. I’ll send the definitions and the dashboard layout we’re using internally.

[06:13] Priya Desai: Will we get those in our view, or is it just for you?

[06:16] Allison Grant: For the POC, we can share screenshots and we can also share aggregated numbers in a weekly report. Customer-exposed UI isn’t ready yet; but we can provide the data and trace exemplars.

[06:29] Jordan Lee: That’s okay, but we need something we can show to our SREs. Even just a CSV is fine.

[06:35] Allison Grant: Yep, we can do that.

[06:37] Sean Gallagher: And on guardrails: we’ll have automated rollback triggers based on p99 regression and error rates, plus compaction budget saturation. If compaction starts “eating” too much time or moving too many bytes per interval, it’s a signal it could be causing stalls.

[06:56] Jordan Lee: Who actually flips the kill switch?

[06:59] Sean Gallagher: For hosted cohorts, SRE on-call can disable it. Runtime also has access. We’ve documented it in the runbook. For your POC, we’ll also communicate the escalation path — like if you see a regression, you page us and we can disable within minutes.

[07:16] Megan Chen: Minutes is okay. We just can’t have it sit broken overnight.

[07:21] Paula Mendes: Yep. And I’ll put that in writing.

[07:25] Priya Desai: Can we talk about success criteria for the retest? Because if we’re going to rerun next week, I want to define what pass/fail is.

[07:33] Paula Mendes: Yes. Let’s do that. You said p99 under 1.2 seconds for ~256 tokens. Is that the primary gate?

[07:41] Priya Desai: It’s the primary one. Secondary is error rate — we want like, basically no shedding. And throughput should not drop.

[07:50] Omar El-Sayed: When you say “no shedding,” do you mean 429 / over-capacity responses?

[07:54] Priya Desai: Yeah. We saw a handful. Not huge, but if compaction makes it worse, that’s a problem.

[08:01] Sean Gallagher: Understood. Part of the compaction strategy is specifically to reduce those worst-case OOM-ish moments, which can trigger request shedding. So we expect it to improve. But we’ll validate.

[08:13] Jordan Lee: Another thing: we care about jitter. Like even if p99 is fine, if it’s spiky it messes up our retries.

[08:20] Sean Gallagher: Good point. We can add a “p99 stability” view — like p99 over time and how often it breaches.

[08:28] Allison Grant: We also can annotate the timeline when compaction runs. It’s supposed to be incremental, but you’ll see small spikes if budgets are too aggressive.

[08:38] Priya Desai: I’m going to ask a naive question: compaction means copying memory around on GPU, right? Doesn’t that just add more work?

[08:46] Omar El-Sayed: It does add some copy overhead, yeah. The trick is it’s budgeted and scheduled at safer boundaries. So it trades occasional massive stalls / fragmentation pain for small controlled maintenance.

[09:01] Megan Chen: And it won’t change outputs, correct?

[09:04] Omar El-Sayed: Correctness-wise it should be transparent. KV content is preserved. We also have tests for cancellation edge cases — that was actually the bug we hit in early canary.

[09:16] Jordan Lee: Cancellation edge case… like user cancels a request mid stream?

[09:20] Omar El-Sayed: Exactly. If a request is being relocated and then it’s cancelled, you can leak pages if you don’t do it carefully. That’s fixed.

[09:31] Paula Mendes: Okay, I want to make sure we capture your blockers explicitly. Megan, can you list them from a product perspective?

[09:38] Megan Chen: Sure. Blocker one: p99 spikes in bursts. Blocker two: we need confidence in rollback and support response. Blocker three: if we’re going to move to Dedicated after this, we need to know it’s not going to behave differently there.

[09:54] Paula Mendes: Great. On Dedicated: the same runtime feature applies. Defaults might be different — like compaction budgets can be tuned — but behavior should be consistent.

[10:06] Priya Desai: We’re also considering self-hosting vLLM in our VPC as a fallback. Not ideal, but it’s an option.

[10:12] Paula Mendes: Totally fair, and we can talk about tradeoffs. Dedicated/VPC with Redwood would give you that isolation without you managing the runtime.

[10:20] Jordan Lee: We also looked at Bedrock. Latency wasn’t great.

[10:23] Paula Mendes: Yep, we hear that a lot for this class of workload.

[10:28] Sean Gallagher: On the “behave differently” part — we’ll also run perf canaries across different pools. The mixed-length burst scenario is now part of our canary suite specifically because of this project.

[10:41] Priya Desai: Good.

[10:43] Paula Mendes: Let’s talk retest logistics. If we enable you in the cohort next week, can you run within 48 hours?

[10:50] Priya Desai: Yes, if we get a heads-up. We can kick off a 6-hour run.

[10:55] Jordan Lee: We want to replicate Tuesday night’s shape. Same ramp pattern, same distribution.

[11:01] Allison Grant: If you can share the exact workload params — concurrency, ramp function, prompt length histogram — that helps us compare apples to apples.

[11:11] Priya Desai: Yeah. We have it in a config file.

[11:14] Paula Mendes: Perfect.

[11:16] Sean Gallagher: Also, please capture trace IDs when you see spikes. That’s the best way for us to prove correlation — e.g., compaction bytes moved spikes vs p99.

[11:26] Jordan Lee: We can do that. Our tracing is OpenTelemetry; we’ll attach request IDs.

[11:32] Paula Mendes: Great.

[11:34] Megan Chen: One more question — will the canary change anything else about the model or the endpoint? Like routing?

[11:41] Paula Mendes: No model change. Same endpoint. It’s runtime-side memory management.

[11:46] Omar El-Sayed: There’s also an eviction policy change, but it should only kick in when memory pressure is high. It’s tier-aware and LRU-ish.

[11:56] Priya Desai: Eviction means… you drop someone’s cache?

[12:00] Omar El-Sayed: In extreme cases, yes. But it’s designed to be safe. Think of it like we choose which sequences to reclaim from rather than failing unpredictably. In practice, the goal is to avoid hitting that path by compaction earlier.

[12:17] Jordan Lee: That’s a little scary.

[12:19] Sean Gallagher: Totally. That’s why it’s coupled with observability and limits. Also, for higher tiers we can configure it differently; for Dedicated you’d have more control.

[12:30] Priya Desai: For the POC, we’re just Hosted, right?

[12:32] Paula Mendes: Correct.

[12:34] Megan Chen: Okay.

[12:36] Paula Mendes: I’m going to jump to the “what we need to do between now and retest.” Allison will send metrics definitions. Sean will send guardrails and who owns kill-switch. I’ll send the schedule.

[12:49] Paula Mendes: Anything else you need from us to run the retest smoothly?

[12:53] Priya Desai: If you can confirm the cohort enablement via email, and ideally we can do a quick ping in Slack when it’s live.

[13:01] Paula Mendes: We can do that. We’ll create a shared Slack channel if you want.

[13:06] Jordan Lee: Yes please.

[13:07] Paula Mendes: Okay.

[13:09] Sean Gallagher: One more thing — when you saw “over capacity,” do you recall the rate? Like how many per minute?

[13:16] Priya Desai: It was low. Like, maybe 0.2% of requests during the burst. But we didn’t dig into if it was retry-able.

[13:25] Sean Gallagher: Got it. We’ll look at it. If it correlates with fragmentation, compaction should help.

[13:32] Omar El-Sayed: Also, what was the max context length you hit in that run?

[13:36] Priya Desai: Some were like 12k tokens in prompt. Most are 2k to 4k.

[13:43] Omar El-Sayed: That’s definitely the regime where fragmentation can be painful.

[13:47] Megan Chen: Can I ask — do you have numbers from your internal canary showing improvement?

[13:52] Paula Mendes: We do, but we’re being careful sharing exact numbers because the cohorts differ. Directionally: it reduces fragmentation ratio and reduces p99 spikes in the mixed-length burst scenario.

[14:05] Allison Grant: And we can share before/after graphs that are anonymized.

[14:09] Megan Chen: That’s fine.

[14:11] Paula Mendes: Okay. Let’s do a quick Q&A. Anything else on your side?

[14:16] Jordan Lee: Just, like, worst case, if it doesn’t work, what’s plan B? Are we just stuck?

[14:23] Omar El-Sayed: If compaction doesn’t sufficiently reduce p99, we have additional levers: adjusting compaction trigger thresholds, budgets, and eviction aggressiveness per tier. Also, we can provision more headroom. But we’re trying to solve it at the allocator level so it’s not just “throw GPUs at it.”

[14:42] Sean Gallagher: From SRE side, we also can shape bursts via rate limit policies, but again that’s not ideal for your use case.

[14:50] Priya Desai: Yeah, we can’t rate limit our users too hard.

[14:54] Paula Mendes: Totally.

[14:56] Megan Chen: Okay, I think that’s good.

[15:00] Paula Mendes: Let me recap and then we’ll end early.

[15:03] Paula Mendes: Recap: POC is looking good on median/p95, remaining blocker is intermittent p99 spikes during burst + long prompts. Redwood believes it’s KV cache fragmentation. Compaction + tier-aware eviction is in canary; you’re not enabled yet. We’ll email cohort timing, share metrics definitions and dashboards, and share rollback/kill-switch authority and triggers. Northwind will rerun the benchmark within 48 hours of enablement and share trace IDs and workload config. Then we schedule a follow-up to decide next steps, potentially Dedicated/VPC scoping.

[15:41] Jordan Lee: Sounds right.

[15:43] Priya Desai: Yep.

[15:44] Megan Chen: Thanks.

[15:46] Sean Gallagher: Thanks all.

[15:47] Omar El-Sayed: Thank you.

[15:49] Paula Mendes: Great. I’ll send notes and next steps today. Bye.

(Recording ends)
